messages:
lee: Noticed a ticket where fncall schema rejects are getting attributed to /chat.generate in the billing UI. Looks like this started after the route-pipeline refactor.

olivia: do you have an example req id? can run a quick trace.

lee: req 7b2a4c99, happened 2025-11-06T09:04:11Z. customer says they called a function, validator rejected output shape, console shows tokens billed under /chat.generate and quota counters incremented there.

cruz: short recap of the pipeline: request enters -> auth -> router-resolve -> validation -> executor -> billing event. router-resolve used to run before validation but we moved it to after in 2025-09 refactor to unify routing for streaming. looks like a side-effect.

olivia: hm. if router-resolve happens after validation, any validator-side early errors will pick up the default route tag (we set default to /chat.generate). that would explain misattribution.

lee: impact? how many events this week? ops-bot, any counts?

ops-bot: dry-run query: 2025-11-05 00:00 to 2025-11-06 12:00 UTC, predicate "validation.error_kind:invalid_function_output AND billing.route:'/chat.generate'" => 328 matches.

cruz: not tiny. customers with dedicated capacity will care about chargeback. we should avoid changing billing semantics without consult but this is clearly wrong.

olivia: mitigation options: 1) move router-resolve back earlier, 2) copy route metadata to a transient header at ingress so validation emits correct tag, 3) post-process billing events to remap by error predicate.

lee: option 3 seems risky for accounting. prefer 2 as minimal invasive. do we have middleware to carry route-id before validation?

cruz: we do have an ingress header x-route-hint used for routing telemetry. it was meant for canary routing. can repurpose it to hold route-id during pipeline. low-risk change: populate at auth stage from the route table and let downstream steps read it.

olivia: that would require small changes in the validator to prefer header over local route context if present. add unit tests. also need to document the header contract.

lee: good. and for customers already impacted we need a backfill: ops, can you produce a mapping of affected reqs grouped by customer so billing teams can reconcile?

ops-bot: backfill plan: generate list for 2025-11-04 -> 2025-11-06. Will produce CSV with req_id, customer_id, original_route, error_kind. Dry-run count 328 as above.

cruz: i'll open a PR for the ingress header population and validator fallback to header. will include flag gate behind feature-flag "preserve-route-before-validate" default off. want canary at 5% first.

olivia: i'll handle tests and add an integration that simulates fncall reject and asserts billing.route == "/fncall" when header is set.

lee: docs: add note to console docs explaining how fncall vs chat billing attribution works and mention the header contract. add a temporary dashboard alert to detect >5 mislabels per hour.

docs: will add small doc and example logs. will also draft a support FAQ for affected customers to explain we will reconcile.

olivia: one more thought: add telemetry flag in the validator to emit route_hint in the validation error payload so billing processors downstream have extra info for remap. small size change.

cruz: agreed. include that in PR. ops: after we deploy canary, run backfill to patch historical events where safe. coordinate with billing to avoid double-charging.

ops-bot: acknowledged. scheduled dry-run job and will notify @billing when PR is merged to start reconciliation window.

lee: thanks all. timeline: PR up today, canary tomorrow, backfill once canary stable. keep me posted.
